newsitem.title: INDIA: INTERVIEW - Motorola sees million pagers in India.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Motorola sees million pagers in India.

text.p: The number of Indian paging subscribers will cross the one million mark by the end of this financial year, a senior official at Motorola Inc said on Thursday.

"About 30,000 subscribers are being added nationally each month. I expect this figure to reach 40,000 to 50,000 subscribers per month by the end of the year," said Percy Batlivala, Executive Director, India Paging at Motorola India Pvt Ltd.

Motorola India has a dominant share of India's paging industry. Earlier this month a joint venture between Motorola, Hong Kong's Distacom and India's Modicorp launched a cellular telephone service in the states of Punjab and Karnataka.
Demand for paging in India was one of the fastest in the world, he said, considering that it was launched only a few months before cellular services, and about a year before radio trunking services.
Paging services started in India in early 1995, after licences for 27 cities were auctioned in 1994 by the Indian government as part of an economic liberalisation programme that was launched in 1991.

The paging industry considers September 1995 as the benchmark for the start of paging services, as at least two operators were up and running in each of the licensed cities. Since then, the industry has been growing by leaps and bounds.

"At the end of 1995, there were a total of 125,000 pagers. This increased to 435,000 by 1996. After crossing a million this year, it should climb to two million in 1998, reach 3.5 million by 1999 and six million by 2000," Batlivala said.

"The biggest change is that pagers are driving further down into the socio-economic marketplace. People like electricians, carpenters and plumbers are realising the need to be accessible and to have a pager."

Another factor driving paging growth is the start of services in about 30 more cities this year. Zonal licensees have already launched services in the southern states of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, and in the northern state of Punjab.

"Zonal licensees have 11,000 subscribers at present. While the bulk of the growth will still come from seven to 10 cities, such as the metros, the zones will start adding numbers from the end of the year, once roaming becomes a need," Batlivala said.
He said the penetration of cellular phones would also play a part in driving the paging market. "The world over, 40 percent of people who have cellphones have pagers," Batlivala said.
India still had a way to go when it came to adopting new technologies such as voice messaging and two-way paging, he said.
Voice messaging enables a subscriber to receive voice messages on a pager. Two-way paging lets a subscriber send short messages, apart from receiving messages.

"A move up the value chain with new paging technologies will only start from next year. This year is a consolidation year for the paging industry. All service providers want to do is to get paging to the people."
